items.followUp: A cyclist travels half a circular track of radius 250 m in 100 s. Find the cyclist’s speed and average velocity.

rubric.why: The time must be converted to seconds for the SI calculations.
rubric.description: Converts the time to 90 s.
rubric.how: Award for identifying or using 90 s.

rubric.why: The distance for half a circle is half its circumference, πr.
rubric.description: Finds the half-circle distance as πr (about 998 m).
rubric.how: Award for the correct formula and distance.

rubric.why: Speed is total distance divided by time.
rubric.description: Finds the speed as approximately 11.1 m/s.
rubric.how: Award for the correct speed with unit.

rubric.why: The displacement for half a round is the diameter of the track.
rubric.description: Finds the displacement as 2r = 636 m.
rubric.how: Award for the correct displacement.

rubric.why: Average velocity is displacement divided by time and has the displacement’s direction.
rubric.description: Finds average velocity as approximately 7.07 m/s along the diameter towards the opposite point.
rubric.how: Award for the correct magnitude, unit, and direction.

modelAnswer: Given: radius r = 318 m; time t = 1.5 min = 90 s.
Distance travelled in half a round = πr = 3.14 × 318 m = 998.52 m.
Speed = distance ÷ time = 998.52 m ÷ 90 s = 11.1 m/s.
Displacement = diameter = 2r = 2 × 318 m = 636 m.
Average velocity = displacement ÷ time = 636 m ÷ 90 s = 7.07 m/s, along the diameter towards the opposite point.
Speed = 11.1 m/s; average velocity = 7.07 m/s along the diameter.
Speed is the distance travelled per unit time; average velocity is the displacement per unit time in the displacement’s direction.

items.followUp: A force acts at 60° to the horizontal. Its horizontal component is 15 N. Find the magnitude of the force.

rubric.why: The given horizontal component must be related to the force using the angle.
rubric.description: Identifies the horizontal component as 20 N and the angle as 30°.
rubric.how: Award for correctly identifying the given values.

rubric.why: For an angle measured from the horizontal, the horizontal component is F cos θ.
rubric.description: Uses the horizontal-component relation 20 = F cos 30°.
rubric.how: Award for the correct component formula and substitution.

rubric.why: Solving for F gives 20 ÷ cos 30° = 40/√3 N.
rubric.description: Finds the force as approximately 23.1 N.
rubric.how: Award for the correct force magnitude and unit.

modelAnswer: Given: horizontal component Fx = 20 N; angle θ = 30°.
Formula: Fx = F cos θ.
Substitution: 20 N = F cos 30°.

items.followUp: A cube-shaped glass block has side 4 cm and mass 140 g. If the density of glass is 2.5 g cm⁻³, find the volume of any cavity inside it.

rubric.why: The cube’s side is needed to calculate its total volume.
rubric.description: Identifies the side as 5 cm.
rubric.how: Award for correctly using the given side.

rubric.why: The volume of a cube is side cubed.
rubric.description: Finds the cube’s total volume as 125 cm³.
rubric.how: Award for the correct cube volume.

rubric.why: The mass and density are needed to find the volume of glass.
rubric.description: Uses the given mass and density in V = m/ρ.
rubric.how: Award for identifying and applying the given quantities.

rubric.why: The glass volume is mass divided by density.
rubric.description: Finds the glass volume as 120 cm³.
rubric.how: Award for the correct glass volume.

rubric.why: The cavity volume is the total cube volume minus the glass volume.
rubric.description: Finds the cavity volume as 5 cm³.
rubric.how: Award for the correct final answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: side of cube = 5 cm; mass of glass = 306 g; density of glass = 2.55 g cm⁻³.
Volume of cube = side³ = (5 cm)³ = 125 cm³.
Volume of glass = mass ÷ density = 306 g ÷ 2.55 g cm⁻³ = 120 cm³.
Volume of cavity = volume of cube − volume of glass = 125 cm³ − 120 cm³.
Volume of cavity = 5 cm³.

items.followUp: What do prefixes indicate when written before units?

rubric.why: Prefixes are written before unit names or symbols.
rubric.description: States that prefixes are placed before units.
rubric.how: Award for indicating their position before a unit.

rubric.why: Prefixes indicate powers-of-ten multiples or submultiples of units.
rubric.description: States that prefixes indicate multiples or submultiples of units.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning multiples, submultiples, or both.

modelAnswer: Prefixes are symbols or names written before units.
They indicate multiples or submultiples of the units.

items.followUp: What is the least count of a measuring instrument?

rubric.why: Least count describes the smallest measurable value of the instrument.
rubric.description: Identifies the least count as the smallest measurement or value measurable.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is the smallest measurable quantity.

rubric.why: The definition must specify accurate measurement by the vernier calliper.
rubric.description: States that this is the smallest length measurable accurately by a vernier calliper.
rubric.how: Award for linking the smallest measurement to accurate measurement with the instrument.

modelAnswer: The least count of a vernier calliper is the smallest length that can be measured accurately with it.

items.followUp: What is a physical quantity? Give one example.

rubric.why: Physical quantities are measurable properties.
rubric.description: States that a physical quantity can be measured.
rubric.how: Award for the measurable property criterion.

rubric.why: A measured physical quantity is expressed by a magnitude and a unit.
rubric.description: States that a physical quantity is expressed with a magnitude and unit.
rubric.how: Award for including both magnitude and unit.

modelAnswer: A physical quantity is a property that can be measured.
It is expressed as a numerical magnitude and a unit.

rubric.why: Vibratory motion repeatedly moves to and fro.
rubric.description: States that the motion is to and fro.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the repeated back-and-forth motion.

rubric.why: The to-and-fro motion occurs about a mean position.
rubric.description: States that the motion is about a mean position.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the position about which the body moves.

modelAnswer: Vibratory motion is the repeated to-and-fro motion of a body about its mean position.

rubric.why: Uniform acceleration means equal changes in velocity in equal time intervals.
rubric.description: States that the velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time.
rubric.how: Award for the equal-change and equal-time condition.

rubric.why: The definition specifically concerns the rate of change of velocity with time.
rubric.description: Identifies velocity as the quantity changing over time.
rubric.how: Award for referring to change in velocity over time.

modelAnswer: Uniform acceleration is the acceleration in which velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time.
